intro: Two years, three universities, one joint degree. Here is the path from your first week in Bologna to graduation.

items.text: Everyone starts at the University of Bologna with four compulsory courses: economics and management, the right to health, quantitative methods (two levels to choose from) and health systems or international law.
The Welcome Days introduce the four tracks. You choose your track at the end of September.
Each track takes at most 35 students, and the Consortium Board decides the final allocation. Once you submit your choice, you cannot change it.
Specialisation courses of your track, usually four to six courses of 5 to 10 ECTS each.
One week, right after the second semester. Coaching on your thesis proposal and on personal skills.
Attendance is strongly recommended; only valid reasons such as illness are accepted. Details come at the start of semester 2, and questions go to the MCI coordinator.
More specialisation courses of your track. You receive the Thesis Guidelines in the summer before.
You can join the MCI Mentoring Programme, which connects you with EU-HEM alumni for career advice. Registration details come at the start of semester 3.
The whole semester is for your thesis. Its topic is linked to your track, and you write it at one of your track's universities.
You may combine it with a research assignment in a company or organisation to collect data.
The Career Event helps with CVs, LinkedIn, job applications and interviews, and is a chance to meet your cohort again.
Each cohort has one graduation ceremony, in the autumn after the second year, where you receive your diploma and diploma supplement. Guests are welcome, up to a limit given in the invitation.
If you finish later and miss the ceremony, you can collect your diploma at Erasmus University Rotterdam or have it posted.

jointDegree.intro: EU-HEM is a joint degree: one diploma with full legal value in all four countries, signed by all four universities. It lists four titles:

titles.title: Laurea Magistrale in Health Economics and Management
Master of Science in Health Economics and Management
Master of Philosophy in Health Economics and Management

items.text: A joint diploma supplement explains the programme, your courses and the different grading systems.
All EU-HEM students are enrolled at Erasmus University Rotterdam, even though everyone starts in Bologna.

events.text: First meetings between the partner universities.
Double and multiple degrees, with six tracks.
Joint degree, after accreditation in Norway (2012), Austria (2014), the Netherlands and Italy (2015).
A joint first semester in Bologna and a revised curriculum with four tracks.
Accreditation by NVAO (the Dutch-Flemish accreditation body) under the European Approach for joint programmes.

erasmus.title: Erasmus+ mobility grant
erasmus.intro: The grant helps with travel and living costs, usually in semesters 3 and 4. The university that pays it (your home university for the grant) depends on your track:

byTrack.text: University of Bologna or University of Oslo, depending on where you defend your thesis

erasmus.caveat: In some cases, students are spread across the partner universities to balance the number of nominations at each one.

items.text: The grant is not guaranteed. You should be able to pay for your studies without it.
The amount depends on things like living costs at home and abroad, the number of applicants and the distance. Each university sets its own rules.
You must live in the country in the semester you receive it. In semester 4 you are enrolled at your thesis supervisor's university, so you can only apply if you will live in that country.
A grant paid by UiO means paying the UiO semester fee (about €80) in those semesters.
At UniBo you apply through AlmaRM, from about early January to early February, and accept the grant on the platform within a few days if selected.
